observation.visible_scene: A transparent glass lens ball rests on a wet pebble beach in the left-center foreground, set against a calm body of water at sunset. The low sun sits on a distant shoreline, painting the sky orange-pink and throwing a shimmering golden reflection column across the water. The ball contains a refracted, inverted image of the sunset with a bright sun spot in its lower-left.
visible_changes: The lens ball remains fixed in the same position throughout the excerpt; it does not roll, slide, or deform.

Small waves and foam lap onto the foreground pebbles: early frames show the stones largely exposed with a thin water film, then a wave edge advances from the water side (around frames 9-16) and washes over the lower stones, after which the water recedes and returns repeatedly (frames 17-30).
By the later frames (31-41) the foreground pebbles are more consistently covered by a shallow sheet of water and patchy foam, indicating ongoing gentle lapping rather than a single wave.

The sun's glitter path on the water and the bright reflection spot inside the ball shimmer and shift in intensity frame to frame, but the sun's position on the horizon and the horizon line itself stay constant.
The camera appears stationary: the ball, horizon, and distant shore hold the same screen positions across all frames, so the visible motion is the moving water, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What drove the wave motion (wind, tide, etc.) is not shown.
The state of the beach before the excerpt and any continuation after the last frame are unknown; the lapping is already underway at frame 1 and still ongoing at frame 41.
Whether the ball was placed there by someone is not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact boundary between water covering a stone and the stone being dry is hard to judge in some mid frames due to the thin reflective film.

The bright point inside the ball is a refracted image of the sun, not a separate light source, but its internal shimmer is too subtle to attribute confidently to water motion versus natural light variation.
